source_user: Choose between tensor and pipeline parallelism for a latency-sensitive multi-GPU service. State the assumptions needed. Scenario variant 92: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: compare per-GPU memory, communication topology, layer partitioning, batch and microbatch behavior, synchronization, latency target, and failure/reconfiguration costs.
corrected_answer:
For scenario variant 92, the prompt is under-specified, so do not select tensor parallelism (TP) or pipeline parallelism (PP) without measurements. Assume a fixed model/checkpoint, precision, GPU count and type, usable memory in GiB, placement/topology, software versions, clock/power policy, request prompt and output-length distributions, offered load, concurrency, batching policy, and explicit p50/p95/p99 end-to-end, TTFT, and TPOT targets in ms. Define throughput units, quality/correctness gates, error and availability budgets, and whether rank failure or reconfiguration is permitted; label unknowns as assumptions rather than platform facts.

Pre-register the hypothesis before tuning: at a named offered load and fixed gates, the selected feasible configuration will reduce held-out p99 end-to-end latency by at least M ms or M% versus the best feasible alternative, without violating memory, quality, error, or availability limits. Enumerate feasible TP degrees and PP layer partitions. For TP, measure shard memory, collective bytes and duration, topology placement, synchronization and straggler waits. For PP, measure balanced per-stage compute, activation memory, inter-stage transfer time, microbatch count, pipeline bubble fraction, queueing, and synchronization. Also measure throughput, TTFT, TPOT, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU memory/utilization/power, network traffic, OOMs, timeouts, retries, dropped requests, and recovery/reconfiguration time with units.

Use randomized interleaved paired trials on identical warmed replicas and the same replayable request trace. Reserve disjoint tuning and held-out traces, repeat enough runs for confidence intervals, and report the effect and uncertainty rather than a single best run. Control warm-up and compilation, caches, clocks, thermal state, placement, software, request mix, concurrency, and batch/microbatch policy; stratify by input/output length and load. For this troubleshooting case, inspect whether communication, stage imbalance, bubbles, queueing, or memory pressure explains any result, and distinguish measured telemetry from estimates.

Adopt only a configuration that passes quality, correctness, memory, error, availability, and latency gates on held-out traffic. Test bounded failure injection (for example a worker loss or timeout) only in an authorized isolated environment, record detection, cleanup, fallback and recovery, and never expose customer data. Canary behind an approved reversible switch, cap load and blast radius, retain the known-good configuration, and roll back on any gate breach, instability, unexpected cost, or failed recovery. Domain-expert review and actual benchmark measurements remain required before treating the recommendation as authoritative.

Assume a fixed model/checkpoint, precision, GPU count and type, usable memory in GiB, placement/topology, software versions, clock/power policy, request prompt and output-length distributions, offered load, concurrency, batching policy, and explicit p50/p95/p99 end-to-end, TTFT, and TPOT targets in ms. Define throughput units, quality/correctness gates, error and availability budgets, and whether rank failure or reconfiguration is permitted; label unknowns as assumptions rather than platform facts.

Pre-register the hypothesis before tuning: at a named offered load and fixed gates, the selected feasible configuration will reduce held-out p99 end-to-end latency by at least M ms or M% versus the best feasible alternative, without violating memory, quality, error, or availability limits. Enumerate feasible TP degrees and PP layer partitions. For TP, measure shard memory, collective bytes and duration, topology placement, synchronization and straggler waits. For PP, measure balanced per-stage compute, activation memory, inter-stage transfer time, microbatch count, pipeline bubble fraction, queueing, and synchronization. Also measure throughput, TTFT, TPOT, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU memory/utilization/power, network traffic, OOMs, timeouts, retries, dropped requests, and recovery/reconfiguration time with units.

Use randomized interleaved paired trials on identical warmed replicas and the same replayable request trace. Reserve disjoint tuning and held-out traces, repeat enough runs for confidence intervals, and report the effect and uncertainty rather than a single best run. Control warm-up and compilation, caches, clocks, thermal state, placement, software, request mix, concurrency, and batch/microbatch policy; stratify by input/output length and load. For this performance analysis case, inspect whether communication, stage imbalance, bubbles, queueing, or memory pressure explains any result, and distinguish measured telemetry from estimates.

Adopt only a configuration that passes quality, correctness, memory, error, availability, and latency gates on held-out traffic. Test bounded failure injection (for example a worker loss or timeout) only in an authorized isolated environment, record detection, cleanup, fallback and recovery, and never expose customer data. Canary behind an approved reversible switch, cap load and blast radius, retain the known-good configuration, and roll back on any gate breach, instability, unexpected cost, or failed recovery. Domain-expert review and actual benchmark measurements remain required before treating the recommendation as authoritative.

quality_dimensions.coverage: covers assumptions, mechanism tradeoffs, boundaries, failure modes, measurement plan, and safety limits
quality_dimensions.technical_correctness: conditional comparison; no unsupported platform claim
quality_dimensions.experimental_rigor: pre-registered hypothesis, randomized paired trials, disjoint holdout, uncertainty and confounder controls

risks: hardware/topology and workload assumptions may not hold
tail latency can be distorted by queueing, batching, or insufficient trace volume
failure testing may be unsafe without explicit authorization
evidence_required: measured memory and communication telemetry for candidate TP/PP configurations
held-out p50/p95/p99, TTFT, TPOT and throughput with confidence intervals
quality/error/availability gate results and authorized recovery test results
